newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Oerlikon sees continued 1997 EBIT growth.
newsitem.headline: Oerlikon sees continued 1997 EBIT growth.

text.p: Swiss arms to fashion conglomerate Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG said annual growth in EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) in 1997 and coming few years should be in the same range as in 1996.

Chairman Hans Widmer told a news conference his forecast referred to the growth in EBIT in 1996 compared with the revised 1995 figures. Oerlikon changed its accounting principles and revised its accounts.
EBIT rose to a revised 204 million Swiss franc in 1996 from 139 million reported the year before for a gain of 65 million.
But applying the same accounting principles to both years, EBIT rose 43 million or 27 percent, Widmer.
"Yes, EBIT will rise in the same range this year as it did last year based on the revised figures," Widmer said.
"In the future EBIT will continue to grow for the next couple of years in the same range as from last year to this year," Widmer said.
He also said that EBIT growth would be lower in the first half of 1997 than in the second half because sales would also be concentrated in the second six months of the year.

Widmer said the lower sales in the first half was based on seasonal business growing toward Christmas at shoe maker Bally and an natural delay between orders and delivery and capital goods manufacturers, Balzers and Leybold, Oerlikon Contraves and Pilatus.

"EBIT accumulation will happen in the second half, parallel to sales. We will not certainly not be able to present a brilliant EBIT for the first half," added corporate finance officer Beat Baumgartner.
